headnotes: My great grandmother's original recipe called for eggs and oil, which I've made optional. If you add egg and oil, it requires a bit less water, and quite a bit more kneading to work properly. But bagels have a very good chewy texture.

steps: Mix fresh, robust starter with tepid water
Pre-mix dry ingredients in a bowl and add to starter/water mix.
Optionally, add oil to the mixture and mix for a few minutes.
Let rest for a few minutes.
Optionally, add eggs and mix thoroughly.
Let rest for at least 30 minutes to come together.
Knead for at least 10 minutes, until dough is firm and "windowpanes".
Let rise at room temp for at least 6 hours. Dough will not double, but should expand.
Knock down air.
Split into ~125g pieces.
Form into tight balls, pinching the bottom and rolling the seams against the counter to seal.
Let balls rest for 10 mins or so, until soft and pliable.

Form into bagels — the easy way: poke your thumbs through the balls and expand. The hard way: roll balls out into long ropes and stretch around the top of your palm, sealing by rolling the joined ends against the counter.
Let bagels proof on trays, covered in towels or plastic (a large bag works well) at room temperature until the bagels expand and get puffy, typically 2-3 hours.
Refrigerate bagels overnight to develop flavor.
Bring water to a boil in a large pot and add 40g (2 Tbsp) sugar or baking soda
Boil bagels one at a time for 1 minute on each side. They should float to the top almost immediately. If they don't, let the bagels sit at room temp for another 30 mins, test, etc.
Remove from water and let rest on a greased, floured, cornmealed, or siliconed tray.
Optional: boil again, 1 minute per side, once bagels have dried for extra crispy crust.
Add toppings (salt, sesame seed, poppy seed, etc.) as desired.
Bake as hot as you can (at least 500º) for 10-15 minutes until slightly brown and crisp
For more even browning, turn every 5 minutes.
Let rest for 30 minutes
Enjoy fresh with toppings of your choice.
Will freeze and taste good toasted — I like to slice them before freezing for easy toasting.

data.title: Bagel

headnotes: True baguettes require lots of steam. You can accomplish this by using a hotel pan and lava rocks at the bottom of the oven and spraying the baguettes liberally with water. But baking without steam will not yield great results.

You'll want to make more starter than usual 10-18 hours ahead of time, probably using white flour with your rye starter. This is essentially making a poolish to give the final dough enough oomph to rise.

Resist temptation and let the loaf rest for at least 30 minutes, preferably an hour, before cutting into and eating.
